subject: Data controls for private deployment — MediCore legal checklist
messages:
From: Anita Rao <anita@medicorehealth.com>
To: jordan_blake@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: privacy@medicorehealth.com
Date: 2026-10-18 09:12 -0700
Subject: Data controls for private deployment — MediCore legal checklist

Hi Jordan / Karthik,

Thanks for the demo last week. Our legal and infosec teams put together a short checklist to confirm how Redwood Private will behave when deployed in our VPC. We're evaluating options where we maintain primary control of customer storage and keys. Can you confirm the following at a high level? If convenient, please reference docs or provide attachments we can circulate to our legal team.

1) Is customer data stored anywhere outside our VPC (object blobs, model inputs, inference outputs, or derived artifacts)?
2) If we use customer-controlled object storage, can Redwood create or retain snapshots/backups outside the bucket we provide?
3) What is the deletion workflow when we terminate service or remove a tenant? We need a proof-of-delete attestation and a target timeline.
4) Where are audit logs (access, admin ops) stored? Can those be kept in our account and exported to our SIEM?
5) How are encryption keys handled? Can we bring our own KMS/HSM and ensure key separation so Redwood cannot decrypt without our key?
6) Do you support disabling cross-region replication for persistent artifacts?
7) Which third parties have access to any customer data in Private deployments?
8) Do you produce SOC 2 / ISO reports and can you share a summary for our procurement process?

We'd like concise answers and any ready-to-share artifacts (diagram, runbook, attestation template). If it's easier to do a short call with legal and infra, we can schedule.

Best,
Anita Rao
VP Legal — MediCore Health
[Attachment: MediCore_Checklist.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Anita Rao <anita@medicorehealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-18 12:30 -0700
Subject: Re: Data controls for private deployment — MediCore legal checklist

Hi Anita — thanks for the clear checklist. Answers below (concise) plus I attached a private-deployment diagram and our internal deletion runbook draft for your review. Happy to expand any point or jump on a call.

1) "Customer data outside your VPC": No. In a Redwood Private deployment we operate the control plane (optional) but persistent customer data (object blobs, model inputs/outputs, checkpoint artifacts you choose to persist) reside only in storage you provision in your VPC. We do not copy persistent customer blobs to Redwood-managed storage by default. Temporary in-memory caches/KV are local to the deployment host and are cleared per the deletion workflow described below.

2) "Snapshots/backups": Snapshots are configurable. By default we rely on snapshots you control (EBS snapshots / S3 versioning in your account). Redwood can be configured to create snapshots, but those snapshots live in your account/bucket and are subject to your snapshot lifecycle policies. We can also configure an option that enables us to manage snapshots on your behalf, but that requires explicit contract terms and is not the default.

3) "Deletion workflow & attestation": We provide a standard tenant-offboarding runbook (attached) with a typical timeline:
   - Step 1: Deprovision live allocation and stop ingestion (t+0).
   - Step 2: Flush and zero sensitive in-memory caches (t+0 — completes within 12 hours).
   - Step 3: Remove application-level references and metadata (t+1 — within 24 hours).
   - Step 4: Delete object storage artifacts per your deletion request or retention policy (t+1 to t+7 depending on retention hold settings).
   - Step 5: If snapshots were created, you can request immediate snapshot purge; otherwise snapshots follow your configured lifecycle.
We issue a "Proof of Deletion" attestation (signed PDF) once the above is completed. For most customers who control storage and snapshots, the attestation confirms Redwood performed the orchestrated operations and that all runtime caches were cleared. If you require cryptographic wipe evidence of underlying disks, we can coordinate a separate process (may require extended timeline).

4) "Audit logs": Audit logs (admin actions, operator access, API calls) can be delivered to a logging endpoint in your account (CloudWatch / S3 / Splunk endpoint). By default logs remain in your account; we do not export them to Redwood-managed buckets. We support forwarding to your SIEM with minimal setup.

5) "Encryption keys": You can BYOK (bring-your-own-key) via your KMS/HSM. Redwood supports using customer-managed KMS keys for data-at-rest and for any service-side wrapping keys. With BYOK ensured, Redwood services cannot decrypt stored objects without your KMS permissions. We document the recommended IAM roles in the onboarding guide.

6) "Cross-region replication": Geo-replication is configurable and disabled by default unless you request a multi-region replication policy. We will not enable cross-region replication of your persistent artifacts without your explicit instruction.

7) "Third-party access": In Private deployments, access is limited to the operators you authorize. We do not engage third-party vendors for PLANE-level access to your data. If any support engagement requires shared access (e.g., remote debug using temporary access), that is done via time-boxed, logged sessions with your approval and you receive the session export.

8) "Compliance reports": Please find the SOC 2 Type II summary attached. For full reports we use an NDA + ATO process; procurement teams can request the full package via our security portal workflow.

Attachments included: redwood_private_data_flow_diagram.pdf, data_erase_runbook_v2.docx, SOC2_TypeII_summary.pdf

Next steps: If this looks good we can produce a short attestation template tailored to MediCore and schedule a 30-minute call with our engineering security lead to walk your infra team through the onboarding checklist. Suggested times Thursday/Friday.

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_private_data_flow_diagram.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Anita Rao <anita@medicorehealth.com>
To: jordan_blake@redwood.com
Cc: privacy@medicorehealth.com
Date: 2026-10-19 10:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Data controls for private deployment — MediCore legal checklist

Jordan — thanks for the quick and helpful response. A couple of clarifications from our side:

A) If Redis/KV or other ephemeral caches are used, do those leave any artifacts in our object storage or in the control plane after the cache flush? We need assurance that ephemeral caches do not persist as logs or debug dumps outside our environment.

B) For snapshots created by Redwood but stored in our account: can your automation tag those snapshots so we can identify and purge them automatically? We want a deterministic purge path that legal can sign off on.

C) For the Proof of Deletion attestation — can you indicate what fields the attestation contains? We typically need: list of deleted paths/buckets, timestamp of deletion, operator id, and a short statement of actions performed.

D) Procurement asked if you can provide a redacted SOC 2 Type II and confirm whether any subprocessor has access to persistent customer data in the Private model.

If you can send a proposed attestation template and the SOC redaction, we can review and move to contracting.

Thanks,
Anita

[Inline: privacy@medicorehealth.com asked to confirm whether any cross-account backups happen automatically — marking for answer below.]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Anita Rao <anita@medicorehealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-20 16:40 -0700
Subject: Re: Data controls for private deployment — MediCore legal checklist

Hi Anita — quick follow-up with specifics we can include in contract language. I've attached a draft attestation template and the redacted SOC summary for procurement. Answers below:

A) Ephemeral caches: Ephemeral caches (Redis, in-process KV, accelerator KV caches) do not write persistent artifacts to your object store by default. We explicitly disable any debug/dump agents in production. If we perform a support debug session that requires dumps, those artifacts are created only with your consent and placed in your bucket or a temporary bucket you approve; all such sessions are logged and included in the attestation.

B) Snapshot tagging: Yes — automation can tag all snapshots/backups with a customer tag (e.g., medi_core:tenant=medicore-123, redwood:managed_by=automation). That tag is visible in your account and can be used by lifecycle policies to trigger automated purge. We'll include recommended tag keys in the onboarding docs.

C) Attestation fields: The draft attestation (attached) includes: tenant identifier, list of deleted object prefixes and snapshot IDs, timestamps (action start/complete), operator audit IDs, deletion methods executed (API delete / lifecycle policy / cryptographic wipe), and a signed operator statement. We can add custom fields if your legal team requires them.

D) Subprocessors & SOC: For Private deployments, no Redwood subprocessors have standing access to your persistent artifacts. Any third-party tools we use for our internal operations do not touch your object storage by default. The redacted SOC summary is attached; for a full report we can initiate an NDA channel for procurement.

Attachments: data_erase_runbook_v2.docx, attestation_template_medicore.pdf, SOC2_TypeII_redacted.pdf, redwood_private_data_flow_diagram.pdf

Proposed next step: I'll schedule a 30-minute call with our security engineer and your infra lead to walk through the attestation and tagging plan. What time window works for you on Friday (10/22)?

Thanks — Jordan
